brief.subject: IRS fixes opportunity zone reporting draft; SBA trims bond rules
brief.headline: IRS Corrects Opportunity Zone Reporting Proposal as SBA Streamlines Surety Bond Rules
brief.dek: The IRS corrected its draft opportunity zone reporting rules, the SBA eased surety bond paperwork, and a tax credit hearing moves to phone-only.
brief.lede: The IRS issued corrections to its proposed rules requiring opportunity zone funds and businesses to file new information returns and investor statements.

sections.heading: Opportunity Zone Reporting Draft Corrected
bullets: The IRS corrected proposed regulations REG-116506-25, first published September 11, 2026; check that you are reviewing the fixed text.
Qualified opportunity funds would file information returns and send statements to investors who dispose of their stakes.
Qualified opportunity zone businesses would furnish statements to the funds holding interests in them, adding a new reporting duty.
The proposal also updates how funds are certified and decertified, which matters for clients who plan to keep fund status.

sections.heading: SBA Eases Surety Bond Paperwork
bullets: The SBA finalized changes to its Surety Bond Guarantee program, reducing what participating sureties must submit and retain.
This matters to small contractors that depend on SBA-backed bonds to bid for work.
The rule also fixes conflicting provisions and revises outdated Preferred Surety admissions requirements.
The Quarterly Contract Completion Report is also being revised under the final rule.

sections.heading: Scholarship Credit Hearing Goes Phone-Only
bullets: The December 15, 2026 hearing on the federal scholarship tax credit rules, REG-117199-25, is now telephonic-only.
The proposal covers a non-refundable credit for qualified contributions to scholarship granting organizations.
Owners and advisers planning to comment in person should prepare to participate by phone instead.

items.title: Rule: Surety Bond Guarantee Program: Streamlining and Modernizing
items.snippet: This final rule makes several changes to the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Surety Bond Guarantee (SBG) program regulations. The rule reduces the burden on participating surety companies for submission and retention of documents. The rule also corrects conflicting provisions, as well as revising the obsolete Preferred Surety admissions requirements and the Quarterly Contract Completion Report.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Information Reporting Regarding Qualified Opportunity Zones and Updated Qualified Opportunity Fund Certification and Decertification Procedures; Correction
items.snippet: This document contains corrections to the proposed regulations (REG-116506-25), published in the Federal Register on September 11, 2026. These proposed regulations would implement new statutory requirements for qualified opportunity funds to file information returns with the IRS and furnish statements to investors who dispose of investments in those entities and for qualified opportunity zone businesses to furnish statements to qualified opportunity funds that hold interests in them.
